reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I have ever had. Her lectures are long and boring. She covers entire units before you even take a test on them. The worst part is that she overcomplicates everything she takes extra steps when the problem has already been solved. You may be able to learn it another way, but her tests are just as confusing. Q-drop now.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. Her lectures are long and boring. She covers entire units before you even take a test on them. The worst part is that she overcomplicates everything, she takes extra steps when the problem has already been solved. You may be able to learn it another way, but her tests are just as confusing. Q drop now.
Exams were nothing like the homeworks and she tries to help. She is a good person and very knowledgeable, but she makes her exam way too hard and they can be a lot simpler.

She is a great prof and will help you if you need it. Lectures are sometimes very bland, would 100% recommend reading the textbook to do well. Tests are pretty hard and doing well on them is not easy (avg was in low low 70's sometimes high 60's). Just study the textbook for a few days and a B is very doable.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is a good professor and it's simply a rigorous course. She accepts feedback and cares about her students. I got a C but I could've tried harder so don't be discouraged by my grade. I recommend her but suggest you truly lock in for this one!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She was sweet, but I do not think her lectures prepared us for her exams. There were no test reviews, so the only "review" you had to go over were McGraw Hill HW(which was nothing like the exam).You do have the opportunity to receive 5 points to your final grade if you show up to class and do the iClicker. Which will end up saving me from a C to B.

Not a bad professor at all, but her lectures are really mind-numbing. If you have her for 202 then you're fine. Tests are reasonably difficult but nothing I didn't realize I'd have known if I studied more. "Quizzes" and homeworks are online/asyncronous and due at 11:59 weekly. Do not get behind, you'll have a bad time catching up.

Dr. Strickland is a great professor! Her lectures are a little heavy and there isn't group work in class but the topics from this class are interesting. She is super willing to help and wants to see you succeed. Attendance is not required but it definitely helps when it comes time for the group projects.
get ready to learn everything without a test review. Tests seemed very different than our homework's which made my life very difficult.

Super sweet prof! I ended with a 103 because of all the extra credit. Her lectures are thorough, and she wants you to succeed. Very helpful during office hours. Don't expect exams to be just like HW, but if you understand the concepts you'll be fine. I never read the textbook and just took notes using her templates. Work hard and you'll be fine!

Graded on 3 exams, homework, and learning curves. Exams were super easy, she curved on at least 2, to my knowledge, and gives 5 whole bonus points on your grade if you show up to class and "participate". One of the easiest classes, legit just studied the learning curves and slides the day before and got an easy A.

As much as I do not like the subject, Professor Strickland is great! Her lectures were easy to follow. Make sure to go to class as there are iclickers and they can really help your grade in the end. The exams were a little more difficult in comparison to her practice problems and homework but if you continuously practice you will be just fine!

I love econ and she was a great prof to take. The tests were easy, exact material she taught in lecture. Sometimes we would get off on a tangent and it was hard to focus in 75 minutes classes, but it was all material taught in previous econ classes. Take her if you need this class for credit, there is minimal homework and plenty of extra credit.

I love Strickland!!! Cannot say enough good things about this course. It definitely requires work (attendance and effort in projects) but it definitely is worth it if you care about learning. Just attend class, take good notes, and participate in class and you'll be good!! She's super understanding and available outside of class for anything.

Honestly, if you just show up to the lectures, this class is extremely easy. With the iClicker extra points I ended up with a 103 in this class, as they add 5 total points to your grade. Tests are all multiple choice. Lectures are very easy to follow and she does reviews before exams. Heavy curves.

I am one of those students who learns better on their own. This class was extremely easy to do so. Did not need to attend class to get an A, just had to review notes. Some of her slides are pretty bad, so look carefully enough. The material was easy however, most other students thought it was challenging. Exams curved to an average of 75

This teacher is amazing and really wants you to pass. There is a lot of extra credit and homework to keep your grade up. There is extra credit for almost every lecture. MAKE SURE to attend; she teaches well. You can pass easily if you keep up with the homework, extra credit, and light studying. Honestly, if you fail the 323 course, youre too lazy.
She is a super nice person and a good teacher.  The class itself is just hard and definitely requires you to put in work to do well in it.

I loved taking this course! Econ 323 is supposed to be one of the harder courses within the AGEC major, but with Strickland it was so beneficial. It was not easy, simply because the material is not easy. The course is very concept heavy. She is genuinely the only reason I was able to understand concepts I needed to get down for my other classes!
Dr. Strickland does not make her lectures engaging or easy to follow. The way she sets up her course on Canvas is also very confusing.
great teacher and cares a lot about you. tests are made simple but there is still a lot of material to study
I took econ323 with her. She is the only reason I'm able to understand concepts in my other coursework. Her lectures are so necessary to attend, she is great at teaching!

ECON 607 - Absolutely one of the worst professors at A&M. Her write out exams do not match the homework/lecture material, and she grades the exams extremely harsh. She's passive aggressive. Students corrected her throughout the semester because she did not fully understand the material she was teaching. Don't take the class, you'll learn nothing.

I would recommend just studying the notes she give in class....the online homework barley helps, you can do it all easy then get to the test and its completely different question and be more similar to the examples done in class. MATERAL IS HARD

She is great person but when it comes to teaching its not that great. Material is very hard so no matter who you take it will be difficult. its way too much to study for one test. I've heard one professor for this class gives old test that are similar to the test at hand so I would take her
reviews.ratingTags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is very sweet and does care about you. However, there are only 3 tests that amount to 75% of your grade, and the lectures are extremely confusing if you don't know exactly what you're doing. I didn't know anyone in the class who knew what was going on besides the people who had personal tutors or some sort of outside help.

Lectures are pretty standard considering the course material. She gives thought-out responses to questions in class and cares about student success. She is easily accessible outside of class and encourages questions before, during, and after class. Reading the textbook helps, but is not necessary as her exams align closely with lectures. Great prof

421 is different than in past years. Now there are no presentations and she gives you the data you need. Now it's four tableau dashboards and 4 podcast responses. Not bad, but they do take some time. No reason you shouldn't get an A, but you need to lecture or know someone who does. Lecture info is necessary because it's all studies on the subject.

Poor teaching methods and exams were excessively difficult. Heavy reliance on curves to compensate for inadequacies in teaching and assessment. Experience was also frustrating due to grading for exams being consistently incorrect, had to go to her office hours to argue my points back everytime.

ECON 607 She is extremely kind and understanding. Go to office hours. One problem is that homework probs and the test questions are not worded similar so it is confusing. A LOT of students got Fs/Ds on the first 2 exams so she made us get half credit for take home redos and the final was a take home. Don't know if that will be the case in future.
reviews.ratingTags: Inspirational--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Taught really well. Final was a take home test so most students who thought would fail the class (after the first test) ended up getting A/B. Lot of homework. Clears doubts and available to resolve doubts.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is the best professor I have ever had. A lot of these students take this class as their first ever masters course and expect it to be easy. The material is not easy, and they take it out on her. I struggled a lot, but she did everything in her power to help me succeed & I ended up getting a B. She is an outstanding professor.

ECON 607 seems daunting but do not fret! Strickland gives the opportunity to earn half of your missed points back after each exam. Final exam was a take home exam. Concepts explained thoroughly in class & the lecture/homework math problems prepare you well for the tests. Definitely need to study a good bit but not an impossible class by any means.

ECON607
Ignore the spammed hate comments!

Strickland is a good, caring professor and you will learn what you need to provided you go to lecture and pay attention (shocker). Homework grading is structured generously. Exams were allowed to be corrected for half points back. If you go to class and do the homework's, no reason you can't get an A.
Terrible. Makes the masters a very discouraging experience

Her teaching style is to make things way harder than they need to be. Get ready to dedicate a good chunk of your time and neglecting other school work to pass this class. Just stay away to save yourself.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I found the projects interesting. You will have to present in class twice. Will learn a new program that's helpful for job market. Helps a lot if needed.
reviews.ratingTags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No idea how I managed an A. Material is relatively difficult, if you don't understand unit1 you'll struggle on the others. Tests average 70s- two tests, one final (she curves all). The end of chapter reviews were a lifesaver. Lectures helped but hard to follow. Weekly homework- not worth much. Go to her office hrs she really cares about helping you

Professor Stickland is very sweet and willing to help her students. The class is hard but that's more due to the nature of the topic and not necessarily her teaching. Three exams but the final wasn't cumulative. Was able to get an A without too much studying.
reviews.ratingTags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Go to class and take notes as she is working on the problems. Go into office hours, can't stress that enough, if you have questions on homework or anything in class related ask her, she will help and it will increase your grade. Remember this is a masters course so its going to be hard but pay attention! Review in-class notes and hws for exams!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is one of those classes that makes school seem like indoctrination. Its not okay to make mistakes. Only 3 tests and they count for 75%. She dumbs down concepts in class but makes them hard on tests. Makes mistakes in exams, yet blames class for not understanding the material. Professor's effectiveness = student's recitation. Results speak!
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I know I may not be the best at economics, but man is this class hard! I have taken several upper-level business classes and this one takes the cake. If you can take an easier professor I would consider doing so! This class only has 3 exams and a few homework assignments. There is not a lot of room for mistakes within her grading rubric.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of my favorite classes at A&M, Strickland is an amazing professor that gives you a clear outline of what is expected of you, her lectures are super interesting and will make you want to go to class. I hope to take her again for other courses that she teaches!

Amazing professor! She cares so much for her students, she encouraged us to ask questions which she loved to answer. Many students performed poorly in this class (no matter the professor), because you cannot memorize how to solve problems, you have to make the effort to actually understand them conceptually. Lectures are interesting & entertaining.

Temple herself is an amazing person and prof, but her class is extremely difficult. Very math heavy as well and often times students in class would correct her on her math, which would further confuse and frustrate the class. Her exams are also extremely tough and the average score of the class was usually pretty low.

I'm awful at economics and hated it, hence my grade. But this woman is phenomenal. I seriously would take her class again just to be in her classroom again. She's caring. Let's you ask questions. She is hilarious. One of the best professors I've ever had. A lot of tenured professors could learn something from her. She also knows how to teach!

Temple is a very nice professor and extremely good at communicating/responding to emails. She was not the best at teaching, though. She was often corrected by other students in class on actual concepts and math. Her exams are extremely difficult for a class that's already difficult enough. The people who skipped class got better grades.

Professor Temple is one of the hidden gems in the econ world. Her exams are extremely difficult (due to the subject) and she does her best to explain and help her students as much as she can. She also makes the effort to get to know her students and what their interests are. She relates content to current events and gives 2 grading scheme options
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Amazing lecturer; she knew all our names and even hobbies in just a few weeks. I attended lectures and did the homework and was scared for exams but fine. Homework software makes the lowest possible grade an 85, but exams are tough (she does curve), very math based rather than conceptual. She encouraged questions and would explain different ways.

Temple is young, so there are lots of references to TV shows/pop culture in the slides, but she is still knowledgeable. Tests really weren't bad, a good mix of math and theory. The HW is on quizlet. Unfortunately, she doesn't show her work in lecture on the ppt online, so you have to go to class to see how to solve the problem (or get it sent to u)

2 test, a final, and homework are all that goes into your grades. She offered selective grading letting you decide if you want your first two tests to be weighted at 25 and letting your final be weighted 35% (homework is 15%) or id you want your first two to be 15% and final at 55%. A little upset because she wouldnt bump me from an 89.4 to a 90.
